name: Little Memory: One Line a Day

ios.desc:
Tried journaling before? Quit after a week? Little Memory is a journal for people who have a hard time keeping a journal. Write one line about your day, that's it. Fifteen seconds, done.

A week, a month, a year from now, your words come back to you. You'll notice patterns you never expected, see how far you've come, and rediscover moments you would have lost.

Featured in Apple Staff Favorites, Dear Diary, and Apps for Writers.

"A clean, beautiful time machine." — App Store review
"If the idea of keeping a journal is daunting, Little Memory is perfect." — Elite Daily

What if there was a simple way to keep the moments that bring meaning to your life? A chance encounter, a first step, a perfect smile: saved in a quiet space that's all your own, and returned to you later, when you need them most. That's Little Memory.

What you get:
■ Memories resurface on their anniversaries: a week, a month, a year later
■ A morning memory: your own words from a year ago, back on your lock screen
■ Nightly reminders and a streak saver, so a good run never slips away
■ Works with Siri: say "Add a memory in Little Memory" to write one without opening the app
■ Your writing time can count as Mindful Minutes in Apple Health
■ Attach photos and note how each day felt
■ Mark your favorites, share a memory as a beautiful card
■ Streaks and stats that show the days adding up
■ A look back at your week, every Sunday
■ iCloud sync across your devices
■ Wide-screen layout for iPad and iPhone Duo
■ Private by design: your memories live on your device and your personal iCloud
■ Export all your memories anytime

Premium:
■ Calendar: flip through every day you've written
■ Search across all your memories
■ Find memories from Spotlight by what you wrote, the day, or the place
■ Unlimited photos: preserve every detail
■ Widgets: a memory from this day, or a quote, on your Home Screen or Lock Screen
■ Photo grids: arrange a day's photos into a collage
■ Tags: organize your memories your way
■ Location: remember where you were
■ Moon phases: see the moon on each day, and search by it
■ Extended insights: the people, places, and feelings your years are made of
■ Automatic Dropbox backup

"The beauty of Little Memory is that it actually restricts you to short entries so keeping up with your journaling doesn't feel like a chore."

"Oscar Wilde said that our memories are the diaries we carry around with us. I love Oscar, but the diary I carry around with me is the Little Memory."

show_hn.title: Show HN: Little Memory 2.0, one-line-a-day journal, offline-first

quotes.text:
I launched Little Memory in 2011 as a Rails app, with the iOS app following in 2012. You write one line about your day, and a year later it comes back to you. Everyone's entries lived in my database, which always made me feel uneasy: if something ever happened to me, someone else would have to keep the servers running just so people could keep using their own diaries. Over the years, people have written over 1 million memories in it.

2.0 is a full rewrite, and it's offline-first. Entries live on the phone (with iCloud sync). You can write in your diary without an account, and your private and personal data stays in your control and in your phone rather than on my servers. It's iOS only, free to download, with a premium upgrade (lifetime/subscription).

The import/migration took the biggest chunk of the project. Many long-time users have thousands of entries. I used to let people add entries via SMS, and running the importer during the TestFlight beta turned up a bug from that: Twilio split long messages into separate webhooks with no shared message ID, and they didn't always arrive in order, so an app designed around one entry per day had been writing two on a single day. The beta found a concurrency bug that silently failed to attach photos, and some people had thousands of photos to import, so I set up background tasks since no one's keeping the app open for long periods of time.

I wrote more about the rewrite here: …
